cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Name Your Backers
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal who supports their position, who authorized it, and who benefits from it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before I tell the workshop staff they're closing, who backed your decision?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director approved it. Please just send the notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I'll name her approval. Who else supported it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sales. They're getting the floor space, but leave them out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then Sales can join the staff meeting. Who signed off on giving them our space?

mechanism: A withholds permission to announce closure until B names the authorizer, supporters and beneficiaries, treating the messenger as accountable downward.
confusable: D54 asks who has practical power; D64 maps the people behind a particular position and their benefit.
comparison: Workshop closure with concealed floor-space beneficiary differs from cheaper roof tiles funding an office refurbishment.
seedUse: Use D64-a director and Sales revelations; make permission to send and omit names conditional on disclosure.
